amelia-customer: Hey team — after the 2026-03-10 deploy we're seeing p99 spikes on sync text-gen calls. TTFB looks normal (~50ms) but total time jumps to 6-8s intermittently. Customer impact: UI freezes. Sample request id: r-0a1b2c3d. Trace: https://traces.internal/r-0a1b2c3d. Repro: single POST to /v1/generate (non-streaming) 2k tokens, occasionally reproduces in our staging.

support-eric: thanks @amelia-customer — can you confirm whether streaming (SSE) endpoints are affected or only non-streaming sync endpoints? any SDKs involved?

amelia-customer: only seeing on sync endpoints (our frontend uses await). We can toggle to streaming but not feasible for all users right now. Using our web SDK v1.4.1. Happened after midday deploy.

maria-eng: pinging infra. tagging request_id r-0a1b2c3d. quick check: is this across regions or single region?

amelia-customer: US-west only.

jonathan-sre: I pulled traces for r-0a1b2c3d. interesting: first byte returned by model service at ~40ms, but client receives final response at ~7.2s. The gap shows buffering at our edge/proxy. Logs show repeated ``[coalesce flush_delay_ms=180]`` entries for that connection.

jonathan-sre: snippet from proxy logs:
```
conn=xyz proto=h2 route=redwood-hosted flush_delay_ms=180 coalesce=true stream_mode=nonstream
... emit chunk size=64kb status=200 trace=r-0a1b2c3d
```

maria-eng: that matches a recent change we rolled to reduce small-packet overhead: default coalesce window changed from 50 -> 180ms to lower token overhead for low-throughput workloads. Side-effect: non-streaming sync responses that rely on immediate flush were delayed for some client paths.

support-eric: are streaming endpoints (SSE / text/event-stream) bypassing that coalesce path?

jonathan-sre: yes — streaming uses immediate-flush path. non-streaming goes through coalescer to form final payload; with long outputs and low token churn that caused large delay. Also some h2 client implementations hold until content-length or EOS; coalescing introduces jitter.

amelia-customer: ok that explains behavior. any short-term fix? customers are getting angry.

maria-eng: mitigation options:
- rollback coalesce default to 50ms (quick, service-wide)
- provide a tenant override flag to force-first-chunk-flush for affected customers
- recommend enabling streaming path temporarily (Accept: text/event-stream) if app can handle incremental responses
- route the tenant to a proxy with legacy settings (canary)

maria-eng: quick repro command (devs):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"long output test","max_tokens":2000,"stream":false}'
```
Expect: first byte quick, final body delayed when coalesce window is high.

jonathan-sre: for an immediate customer-facing workaround we can apply a tenant override to disable coalescing for amelia-customer's org id. I can push that change in ~10m and monitor p99.

ops-bot: deploy started: https://deploys.internal/deploy/33421 (canary 1/5 nodes).

maria-eng: FYI we'll hold rollback if per-tenant override works; rollback impacts unit economics improvements we just shipped. Prefer targeted override + telemetry to confirm.

support-eric: @amelia-customer we'll flip the tenant override now and loop back in 15m. Can you confirm when you see improvement?

amelia-customer: got it — testing now.

(10m later)

amelia-customer: quick update — p99 dropped from ~7.2s to ~220ms for the same test. Huge improvement, thanks.

support-eric: great. leaving notes for follow-up:
- root cause: proxy coalescing window increased in deploy to improve throughput/cost for low-rate workloads; unintended side-effect on sync/non-streaming endpoints causing p99 regression for certain client paths.
- mitigation: per-tenant coalesce disable + customer communication.
- long-term: we should add heuristics to bypass coalescer when response is > X tokens or when request has header ``Prefer: flush-first-chunk``. Also add a perf test for sync path to detect regressions.

maria-eng: opened follow-up tickets:
- INF-7201 add tenant override + API (prio P0)
- INF-7202 add request-level hint ``Prefer: flush-first-chunk`` (P1)
- INF-7203 perf test for sync endpoint p99 (P0)

links: https://issues.internal/INF-7201 https://issues.internal/INF-7203

jonathan-sre: I'll also add a temporary dashboard showing coalesce window vs p99 by tenant so we can catch future regressions before customers escalate.

amelia-customer: thanks everyone — shipping this change for our users now. Appreciate the fast turnaround. :heart:

support-eric: closing loop here; reach out if any regression. we'll follow up with scheduled rollback plan if override doesn't scale. :thumbsup:
